scope: Tiny randomly initialized GPT-2/GPT-NeoX CPU FP32 adapter and intervention validation only; no model download, full-size model, GPU, training or scientific run
decisions: Clean calls delegate to the pinned Transformers 5.3.0 eager model without replacing parameters or modules.
Differentiable pre-dropout FP32 probabilities and projected Q/K/V are purely recomputed from returned layer inputs; no global collector or auxiliary side effect is used.
Causal calls transactionally replace selected attention forwards and edit normalized probabilities before dropout and value aggregation, restoring instance state in finally.
Delete uses a fresh conditional masked softmax of original scaled scores, so saturated sink rows do not divide by one minus sink mass and no uniform fallback exists.
Padding queries are excluded from valid edges and left unchanged; q0 and length-one rows remain unchanged when no valid alternative/destination exists.
Package-level model exports are lazy so the Stage00 dependency-free offline wheel import remains valid.
invariants_verified: GPT-2 fused Conv1D QKV layout, scale flags, absolute-position behavior and tied input/output embeddings
GPT-NeoX fused Linear QKV layout, native rotary Q/K, unrotated V and parallel residual path
native causal/key padding support and explicit exclusion of padded query rows from valid edges
normalized FP32 probabilities before attention dropout and differentiable student Q/K/V/probability paths
native versus adapter clean/no-op forward and parameter-gradient parity
delete, relocate, explicit no-op and strength-zero edits before P@V with analytic downstream change
row sums, nonnegativity, causal support, q0, padding, length-one, doses and saturated-sink stability
integer native-layer scopes and exact mapped-teacher subsets, including generic key1 deletion support
returned attention tuple edits do not change already computed logits; causal adapter edits do
attention forward, parameters, modes and hooks restore after normal completion and forced exceptions
activation checkpoint recomputation matches direct feature gradients without duplicated feature side effects
